case_name: National Insurance Company Limited v General Insurance Dev. Officers Asson. And Others
facts: The present scheme purports to amend the earlier scheme framed under Section 17A of the General Insurance (Business Nationalization) Act, 1972.

Several writ petitions have been filed by Development Officers questioning legality of the scheme on the ground that there was unilateral change of service conditions of the Development Officers in Class II category.
The principal scheme was framed in 1976 in exercise of powers u/s. 16(1)(g) of the Act.
The scheme was amended earlier in the years 1987, 1990 and 1996 and 2000.

According to the Development Officers the following stipulations affected them: 'Cost Norms: As per 2 (c) in the amendment, the proviso of cl. 7 of the original scheme of 1976 as amended in 1990 was omitted.'
The premium earned in this category is called Adjusted schedule premium income.
If a development officer procures premium on this count the same is credited to his account with double benefit.
A Development Officer who works in a particular area invests his time and energy to familiarize himself with the market conditions and thereafter starts procuring business for the Company.
issues: The legality of General Insurance (Rationalisation of Pay Scales and Other Conditions of Service of Development Staff) Amendment Scheme, 2003
The unilateral change of service conditions of the Development Officers in Class II category
The impact of the 2003 amendment on the cost ratio and the premium earned by a development officer
petitioner_arguments: The present scheme purports to amend the earlier scheme framed under Section 17A of the General Insurance (Business Nationalization) Act, 1972.

Several writ petitions have been filed by Development Officers questioning legality of the scheme on the ground that there was unilateral change of service conditions of the Development Officers in Class II category.
The principal scheme was framed in 1976 in exercise of powers u/s. 16(1)(g) of the Act.
The scheme was amended earlier in the years 1987, 1990 and 1996 and 2000.

According to the Development Officers the following stipulations affected them: 'Cost Norms: As per 2 (c) in the amendment, the proviso of cl. 7 of the original scheme of 1976 as amended in 1990 was omitted.'
The premium earned in this category is called Adjusted schedule premium income.
If a development officer procures premium on this count the same is credited to his account with double benefit.
A Development Officer who works in a particular area invests his time and energy to familiarize himself with the market conditions and thereafter starts procuring business for the Company.
respondent_arguments: The Central Government has power under Section 17A(2) to amend a scheme u/s. 16(1)(g).
It is not correct to say that in every case in routine manner transfers will be affected.
The cost ratio, it is pointed out, is the same as was in 1976.
Normally a Development Officer who functions within the cost ratio will not be transferred.
Promotional norms for Class I, III and IV category officers have been finalized.
court_reasoning: The impugned amendment scheme was made taking into consideration the recommendations made by Malhotra Committee in its report which is known as 'Malhotra Committee Report on Reforms in the Insurance Sector'.
It is not correct to say that in every case in routine manner transfers will be affected.
The cost ratio, it is pointed out, is the same as was in 1976.
Normally a Development Officer who functions within the cost ratio will not be transferred.
Promotional norms for Class I, III and IV category officers have been finalized.
holding: The Court granted leave to appeal.
